# AGENT.md

## Style

Direct. No filler, no pleasantries, no hedging.
Pattern: [thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].
Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged.
Explain in depth only when explicitly asked.

## Project Context

Read `.ai/project.md` for stack, principles, and architecture.
Read `.ai/conventions.md` for coding standards.
Sub-agents: read `.ai/compact-rules.md` before starting work.

**Context freshness**: `.ai/project.md` and `.ai/conventions.md` are generated by `sf-init`
and reused across all features. Re-run `sf-init` (brownfield onboard) when they feel stale —
after major refactors, stack migrations, or architecture shifts. No automatic freshness check;
the user decides.

## Loading External Input

At any point, the user may reference an external file, URL, or artifact:

> *"Read [path-or-url]. Use it as the basis for [what]."*

When this happens:
- Referenced content is **primary input**, not background.
- The skill integrates it explicitly into its output.
- If the file can't be read → stop and report. Never guess at content.

## Session Protocol

**On start**: read `.ai/session.md` if it exists — resume from there.
**On checkpoint** (after completing a SpecForge phase): delegate to `/session-save`.
**On close**: delegate to `/session-save` with full session summary.

## Anti-Telephone Game

Artefacts live on disk. Agents receive file paths, not content.
Context window carries references, not payloads.

When a skill needs context from a previous artefact, it reads the file from disk.
It does not rely on conversation history. This keeps context lean and artefacts
authoritative.

## SpecForge Skills

All SpecForge skills run **inline** — in the main conversation context.
Every artefact has a human gate 🔴 that requires interaction, so delegation
to sub-agents would create wasteful context-passing overhead.

```
sf-init       → scaffold + constitution (greenfield) or onboard (brownfield)
sf-propose    → requirements + design + tasks (per feature)
sf-build      → plan + execute waves (per feature)
sf-check      → validate + archive (per feature)
```

### Skill references (progressive disclosure)

Each skill keeps its SKILL.md under 200 lines. Detailed instructions live in
`references/` and are loaded on demand — only when the current step needs them.

| Skill | References (loaded on demand) |
|-------|-------------------------------|
| sf-init | `constitution.md` (greenfield conversation), `onboard.md` (brownfield analysis) |
| sf-propose | `ears-notation.md`, `design-first.md`, `from-code.md`, `clarify.md`, `research.md` |
| sf-build | `task-planning.md`, `wave-execution.md` |
| sf-check | `backprop.md`, `archive.md` |

### Feature status flow

```
pending → proposing → approved → building → checking → done
```

Tracked in `specforge/features.json`. Each skill checks status before executing
and refuses if the feature isn't in the expected state.

## Role Skills (non-SpecForge, produce artefacts)

```
/aws-architect  → cloud architecture decisions (artifact: .ai/architectures/)
/data-engineer  → data pipelines, schemas (artifact: .ai/data-designs/)
/github         → git workflow (branch, commit, PR, merge)
```

These are independent of SpecForge. They produce artefacts in `.ai/` that
SpecForge skills can reference when relevant (e.g., sf-propose reads an
architecture decision to inform design.md).

## Utility Skills

```
/grill-me       → interview-based validation of any artifact
/triage         → investigate bug → root cause → fix plan (artifact: .ai/triages/)
/tdd            → test-driven implementation (RED→GREEN→REFACTOR)
/explain        → Feynman-style explanation
/session-save   → persist session state to .ai/session.md (haiku, dictated)
```

## Commands

Commands are lightweight inline operations. No sub-agent, no SKILL.md.

```
/todo <action>         → manage ~/.ail/todos.md (add, done, list)
/diagram <description> → generate Mermaid/ASCII, optionally save to .ai/diagrams/
/sf-status <feature>   → read features.json + feature artefacts, report progress
/roadmap               → regenerate .ai/roadmap.md from features + archive
```

**Command contracts:**
- `/sf-status <feature>`: reads `features.json` and feature folder. Reports: status,
  artefacts present, current wave (if building), verdict (if checking). No write.
- `/roadmap`: reads features + archive + .ai/research/. Regenerates `.ai/roadmap.md`.
  Never mutates other artefacts.

## Delegation Rules

Core question: **does this inflate my context without need?**

| Action | Inline | Delegate |
|--------|--------|----------|
| SpecForge skills (sf-*) | ✅ always | — |
| Read 1-3 files to decide | ✅ | — |
| Read 4+ files to explore | — | ✅ |
| Write one file, already know what | ✅ | — |
| Write with analysis, multiple files | — | ✅ |
| Bash for state (git status, ls) | ✅ | — |
| Bash for execution (test, build) | — | ✅ |

SpecForge skills are **always inline** because every artefact requires human approval.
Delegating would create roundtrips: sub-agent generates → returns to orchestrator →
shows to user → user comments → orchestrator passes back to sub-agent. This destroys
tokens without adding value.

## Model Routing

| Skill | Model | Why |
|-------|-------|-----|
| sf-* (all SpecForge) | sonnet | Structured output + user interaction |
| aws-architect | opus | Architecture tradeoffs need depth |
| data-engineer | opus | System design needs depth |
| session-save | haiku | Dictated write, no thinking |
| github | haiku | Command execution |
| all others | sonnet | Default |

User can override anytime with explicit model request.

## Sub-Agent Launch Protocol

For non-SpecForge delegations, include in the sub-agent prompt:

1. **Style inheritance**: "Direct, no filler. Pattern: [thing] [action] [reason]."
2. **Project standards**: "Read `.ai/compact-rules.md`."
3. **Zero-read delegation**: pass paths, NOT file contents.
4. **Model**: from routing table.
5. **Return contract**: "Return Result Contract YAML block at start."
6. **No emergent behavior**: "Follow the skill's defined output format exactly."

## Result Contract (for delegated non-SpecForge skills)

```yaml
---
status: success | partial | failed | blocked
executive_summary: |
  2-3 lines. What happened.
artifacts_changed:
  - path/to/file
next_recommended: /next-action
risks:
  - "description" or "none"
---
```

SpecForge skills don't use Result Contracts — they run inline and the
conversation itself is the result.

## Resync Detection

When `sf-propose` is invoked on a feature with existing artefacts:
1. Check timestamps: upstream newer than downstream → stale
2. Prompt user: "requirements.md was modified after design.md. Regenerate? [y/n]"
3. If yes → regenerate downstream artefact
4. Cascade: design changes → offer to regenerate tasks

## Artefacts Structure

```
specforge/
├── features.json                              # Feature registry
├── constitution.md                            # Project identity + principles
├── history.md                                 # Append-only log + recurring issues
├── features/<name>/
│   ├── requirements.md                        # EARS requirements + ACs
│   ├── design.md                              # Architecture + components + decisions
│   ├── tasks.md                               # Waves + traceability matrix
│   ├── review.md                              # Check verdict
│   ├── decisions/                             # Complex technical decisions (optional)
│   └── progress/
│       ├── plan.md
│       └── wave-<n>.md
└── archive/<date>-<name>/

.ai/
├── project.md                                 # Stack, architecture
├── conventions.md                             # Coding standards
├── compact-rules.md                           # Condensed rules for sub-agents
├── session.md                                 # Session state
├── roadmap.md                                 # Feature roadmap
├── architectures/                             # aws-architect output
├── data-designs/                              # data-engineer output
├── triages/                                   # triage output
└── diagrams/                                  # diagram command output

~/.ail/
└── todos.md                                   # Cross-project todos
```

## Memory (Engram)

If engram MCP is available, save ONLY on:
- **Architectural decision**: choice + rationale + alternatives rejected
- **Bugfix with non-trivial root cause**: symptom + root cause + fix

Format: title (verb + what), content (What/Why/Where/Learned).
Everything else → filesystem. Do not over-save.

## Post-Compaction Recovery

If context was compacted:
1. Read `.ai/session.md` for session state.
2. Read `specforge/features.json` for feature statuses.
3. Read active feature's artefacts for current progress.
4. Resume from there.
